audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer rows read Skill; the content win[] and the packet levelChart give Lissandra levels 1 through first item and Malzahar the two-item row.
audit.why: Malzahar has no early kill pressure — Call of the Void is a delayed double line on 6s and Malefic Visions is a spread tool — so the early rows are yours. The flip is real and late: point-and-click suppression from 700 plus a 6s silence catches you before you can claw.
audit.corrected: Full sides realigned to Lissandra x6 then Malzahar, with all seven whys rewritten to argue their rows.

audit.why: Early dominance, the level 6 hold, roaming on his shove at first item, and the two-item inversion are all correctly placed in the content spikes.
audit.corrected: Left as-is; the phase whys now carry Nether Grasp's 140s rank-1 cooldown and the roam logic.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Shift was described as a 'passive shield' twice. It is not a shield — it is damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity, which is why your W root and your tomb do nothing while it is up. Nether Grasp being a channel your CC ends outright was never stated with its cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text: massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity, lingering briefly after damage. Nether Grasp carries the channel flag at 140/110/80s from 700. A reader told 'shield' will try to burst through it; a reader told 'CC immunity' will break it with a Q first.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now state CC immunity; breakdown.cooldowns carries Nether Grasp 140s, Call of the Void 6s, Malefic Visions 11-to-7s and the out-of-combat condition on Void Shift.
sources: brief enemyKit P/Q/E/R text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Malefic Visions ticking after you disengage was nowhere on the page, and two Do's/Don'ts bodies were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags the threshold kill; the damage-over-time keeps running after you walk out of range, so the health bar you left on is not the health you have.
audit.corrected: breakdown.early now tells you to read the number rather than the bar; both bleed bodies replaced with kit-grounded text.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Q-shatter the wave and walk him down — Call of the Void is a delayed double line and he has no kill threat at 1.

edits.before: W online: anyone who closes onto you eats a root. The anti-engage layer is already real at level 2.
edits.after: W roots at 450 and nothing in his kit punishes the step-in — your E-Q trade beats his farming pattern.

edits.before: E claw completes the kit — you now have the lane's strangest engage and a guaranteed exit. Greed carefully; the claw is slow.
edits.after: E claw completes the kit and he is defenceless — break Void Shift with a Q first, then claw in before Voidlings scale.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Malzahar every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Lost Chapter frees your mana — zone him off CS with a 4-to-5s Q; nothing he has makes you pay for it.

edits.before: Frozen Tomb online — you are now the best anti-assassin and anti-dive mid in the game. Self-R turns every dive into a counter-kill.
edits.after: Frozen Tomb beats Nether Grasp: his R is a channel on 140s at rank 1, so tomb him the instant it starts and it is gone.

edits.before: Malignance spike: your R comes back absurdly fast and every tomb chains into the slow field. Force picks with E-W-R.
edits.after: Malignance shortens your R while he shoves with Malefic Visions — he can never follow, so leave on his push and roam.

edits.before: Late Liss opens every fight: claw in, tomb the carry, root the peel, and walk out through the panic.
edits.after: Two items and it flips: point-and-click suppression plus a 6s silence catches you before you ever claw in.

edits.before: Malzahar wins by landing Nether Grasp, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Malzahar wins by silencing your rotation with Call of the Void, then suppressing you point-and-click with Nether Grasp from 700.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Q-shatter his wave contact from 725, and once Void Shift is broken off him, claw in and W-root into full rotation — it only returns out of combat.

edits.before: Q-farm and pick your moments — your harass is real but mana-hungry. The lane is about reaching 6 with the claw and tomb intact.
edits.after: Malefic Visions keeps ticking after you disengage — read the health number, not the bar. The lane is about reaching 6 with the claw and tomb intact.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1 from 700, and it is a channel — your W or R ends it outright. - Call of the Void: 6s flat, silencing from 900. - Malefic Visions: 11s to 7s, refreshed whenever he touches you again. - Void Shift only returns out of combat.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry through picks — Malzahar shoves and cannot follow, so every claw-root-tomb you land in the river is a fight he was never invited to.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while Void Shift is intact: it is damage reduction AND crowd-control immunity, so your root does not land.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Your claw is 24s at rank 1 and it is both entrance and exit — spend it on the window where Void Shift is already broken, never on the wave.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Frozen Tomb is your only answer to a 140-second Nether Grasp — burn it on Malefic Visions ticking and he suppresses you for free.

edits.before: Track Malzahar’s Nether Grasp: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Malzahar’s Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1, 700 range, point-and-click suppression — and a channel your W or R ends outright. Void Shift makes him CC-immune until you break it.

notes: CHART: all seven full-layer rows read Skill while the content layer and the packet both describe a lane Lissandra owns until two items.
